national_raw_news.title: 9 mins ago | National 22 PM Modi announces free online coaching for competitive exams aspirants to ease financial burden o...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has announced to provide free online coaching for students belonging to poor and middle class families. In his address to the nation, Mr Modi said, the move is aimed at easing the financial burden of aspirants preparing for competitive exams. He said, this is a revolutionary step towards making quality education accessible to everyone, led by top teachers. He said, this will save thousands of crore rupees of middle-class family in coaching classes. The Prime Minister said that the government has decided that one crore youth will be given training in AI skilling in the next one year. He said this will enable them to take the lead in the global AI sector. Mr Modi said the country has to focus on three things – cost, quality and skill. Prime Minister said a talent hunt will be launched across villages, cities and schools to identify talent among children aged five to 15 years. He said, the children’s talent will be identified, and they will be given special training to help them become good players for the country. He said, today India is making its place in the world of sports. Mr Modi said, in 2030, India will host the Commonwealth Games.

national_raw_news.title: 19 mins ago | National 14 SURYAPATH TIRANGA Global Relay concludes after journey across 54 countries
national_raw_news.content: The first-of-its-kind SURYAPATH TIRANGA Global Relay concluded yesterday, completing its journey from Fiji in the East to the United States in the West, across 54 countries and multiple time zones. The External Affairs Ministry said that the Suryapath Tiranga initiative was celebrated as part of the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign. Launched from the High Commission of India in Fiji, the relay carried the spirit of the Tiranga from one sunrise to the next, bringing together the Indian community and friends of India across the world. The relay ended with the flag hoisting by the Consulate General of India in San Francisco. The relay also marked 150 years of Vande Mataram, celebrating its enduring legacy as a symbol of India’s national spirit and pride. The relay witnessed overwhelming participation and response from the members of the diaspora, underscoring the deep emotional connection with the Tiranga.

national_raw_news.title: 22 mins ago | Sports 6 Magnus Carlsen wins Esports World Cup chess title for second consecutive year
national_raw_news.content: In Chess, World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen has won Esports World Cup title for the second year in a row, by defeating Belarusian Grandmaster Denis Lazavik 2-0 in Paris, France. Representing Team Liquid, the 35-year-old Norwegian remained completely undefeated throughout the entire tournament. Meanwhile, American Grandmaster Hikaru Nakamura secured third place after defeating Alireza Firouzja 4-1 in a chaotic bronze-medal match that was repeatedly disrupted by technical problems and internet disconnections. The championship layout followed a best-of-three sets format, where the first two sets featured four games each, and a final two-game set was reserved as a tiebreaker if needed.

national_raw_news.title: 11 hours ago | National 422 Independence Day celebrations: PM Modi announces target of 100 Giga Watt Nuclear capacity by 2047
national_raw_news.content: The nation is celebrating the 80th Independence Day today. Prime Minister Narendra Modi led the celebrations at the iconic Red Fort in Delhi. The Celebrations commemorated 150 years of the enduring legacy of the National Song ‘Vande Mataram’. For the first time, ‘Vande Mataram’ was rendered during the celebrations at Red Fort. Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort, Prime Minister Modi said, the government is moving forward with the aim of 100 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity by 2047. Mr. Modi said over the past 12 years, the determination and dedication of crores of citizens have helped take the country to new heights. He said 25 crore people have come out of poverty during this period. Mr Modi said India, once counted among the Fragile Five economies, has now emerged as a major and the fastest-growing economy in the world. He said India has set an ambitious goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047. On the occasion, the Prime Minister announced free online coaching for poor and middle-class families preparing for various public examinations. He also announced that the government will provide AI-skilling training to one crore youth over the next one year. Highlighting the government’s focus on critical minerals, Mr Modi said modern technology depends entirely on these minerals and India is actively working to secure its position in the sector. The Prime Minister said, energy security is one of the major requirements of the present times and the government has taken several significant steps in this direction. He said nuclear energy is an important means of ensuring a country’s energy security. Mr. Modi said the government is moving forward with the aim of 100 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity by 2047. In his address, the Prime Minister called upon the nation to harness the seven streams of strength called as Sapt Dhara. He said, in the next five to seven years, the country will achieve all that could not be achieved in the past five to seven decades.

national_raw_news.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says India-US ties stronger than ever
national_raw_news.content: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio extended congratulations to the people of India on Independence Day. In his message, Mr Rubio said that the India-US relationship continues to grow and is stronger than ever, thanks to the personal relationship between US President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He added that bilateral collaboration is making both nations and the broader Indian Ocean region safer, stronger, and more prosperous. He further stated that the deep ties of friendship and family between people from both countries form the foundation of a partnership that is innovative, resilient, and forward-looking. He said the US looks forward to the future the two countries will build together. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar thanked Secretary Rubio for his warm wishes. Dr Jaishankar also expressed gratitude to his counterparts from Australia, Slovakia, Cyprus, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Singapore for their Independence Day wishes.

national_raw_news.title: Sports Minister interacts with MY-Bharat NSS volunteers; encourages them to participate in building Viksit Bharat 15 Aug 2026 | 8:46 PM 66
national_raw_news.content: Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya today interacted with MY Bharat-NSS volunteers during the Independence Day celebrations in New Delhi. Addressing the volunteers, Dr Mandaviya appreciated their contribution towards social service and encouraged them to actively participate in initiatives aimed at building a Viksit Bharat. He emphasised that the energy, commitment and innovative ideas of young people are essential for achieving the vision of a developed and self-reliant India. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the programme also provided a platform for volunteers to share their experiences, ideas and aspirations. The interaction reaffirmed the commitment of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to provide meaningful opportunities for youth participation and leadership in nation-building. Around 500 students participated in the event, showcasing patriotism, national unity and collective participation.

national_raw_news.title: Country’s exports register robust growth of over 13% in July 13 Aug 2026 | 8:45 PM 325
national_raw_news.content: The country’s total exports, including merchandise and services are estimated at 80.14 billion US dollars in July this year, registering a robust 13.3 per cent year-on-year growth. According to the provisional data released by the Commerce Ministry, the export performance was led by merchandise shipments, which jumped over 19.6 per cent to 44.24 billion US dollars from a year earlier. The growth in merchandise exports was driven by petroleum products, electronic goods, engineering goods, organic and inorganic chemicals, cotton yarn and handloom products. Country’s merchandise trade deficit widened by 31.5 per cent year-on-year to 15 billion US dollars last month. Cumulatively, merchandise exports during April to July period of the current financial year are estimated at 173.78 billion US dollars, registering an increase of 17 per cent on an annual basis.

national_raw_news.title: Asian markets in gain, and European indices show mixed response 13 Aug 2026 | 5:45 PM 340
national_raw_news.content: In the Asian markets, South Korea’s Kospi index gained almost 3.6 per cent and Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose around 1.2 per cent. Among the major European indices, Germany’s DAX was trading 0.4 per cent up, while London’s FTSE 100 dropped 0.3 per cent, when reports last came in. On economic front, United Kingdom’s real gross domestic product (GDP) is estimated to have increased by 0.4 per cent in April to June quarter of this year, down from growth of 0.6 per cent in the first quarter. Meanwhile, GDP grew by 0.3 per cent in June, after registering no growth in the previous month, according to the GDP figures released today by the Office for National Statistics.

national_raw_news.title: Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan to begin two-day visit to Tamil Nadu today 39 mins ago 32
national_raw_news.content: Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan will be on a two-day visit to Tamil Nadu beginning today. During the visit, he will participate in a series of academic, commemorative, and literary events in Chennai, Chengalpattu, Thiruvarur, and Thanjavur. Today, Mr Radhakrishnan will attend the 22nd Convocation of the SRM Institute of Science and Technology in Chengalpattu. He will also attend the first death anniversary function of former Governor of Nagaland, Manipur and West Bengal, in Chennai. Later, the Vice-President will attend the release of the book ‘Echoes of a Nationalist Mind’ in Chennai. The book is based on the thoughts and writings of the late K. Ramagopalan, founder of Hindu Munnani. Tomorrow, the Vice-President will attend the 11th Convocation of the Central University of Tamil Nadu in Thiruvarur. He will thereafter participate in the Ruby and Silver Jubilee Valedictory Celebrations of SASTRA Deemed University at Thanjavur.

national_raw_news.title: 12-day Shri Buddha Amarnath Yatra 2026 to begin tomorrow 49 mins ago 33
national_raw_news.content: The 12-day long annual Shri Buddha Amarnath Yatra 2026 to the ancient Baba Budha Amarnath Temple in Rajpura village of Mandi Tehsil in Poonch district is scheduled to begin tomorrow and will continue until August 28, 2026, culminating around Raksha Bandhan. The first batch of the pilgrims will depart from the Bhagwati Nagar Yatri Niwas in Jammu toward the border district of Poonch tomorrow. Authorities have enforced strict multi-tier security and surveillance across Poonch, Rajouri, and transit routes. The convoys of the devotees will move under police escort, with additional Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) deployed. District administration and local bodies have finalised arrangements, including water proof tents, community kitchen (Langar) locations, parking layouts, and health care stations along the pilgrimage route. The Poonch district administration launched a dedicated portal to facilitate advance registration for pilgrims coming from across the country. The Budha Amarnath Yatra is an annual Hindu pilgrimage held during the auspicious monsoon month of Shravan (July-August) to the ancient Baba Budha Amarnath Temple dedicated to Lord Shiva located in Rajpura village in Mandi Tehsil of Poonch district. The shrine sits 4 thousand 600 feet above sea level and features a self-manifested white stone Shivling. The journey traditionally commences from the Bhagwati Nagar base camp in Jammu, taking pilgrims about 230 km northwest into the mountainous terrain of Poonch. Devotees traditionally bathe in the nearby holy Pulastya River (named after Rishi Pulastya) before entering the temple for prayers. Many believe completing this yatra adds profound completeness to a devotee’s broader pilgrimage path to the higher-altitude Amarnath Cave shrine.

national_raw_news.title: Independence Day celebrated across the country with national pride and patriotic fervour 15 Aug 2026 | 9:17 PM 52
national_raw_news.content: The 80th Independence Day was celebrated in Maharashtra with patriotic fervour. National flag hoisting ceremonies were held at official functions across the state. Addressing the people on the occasion, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis highlighted the government’s commitment to development and welfare, particularly for farmers, workers, women and the youth. The celebrations also carried a message of collective responsibility towards building a stronger and more developed Maharashtra. Meghalaya Governor C.H Vijayashankar hoisted the traditional Independence Day ‘At Home’ reception at Lok Bhavan, Shillong today, bringing together dignitaries and representatives from all walks of life to mark the 80th Independence Day of the country. The programme formed part of the customary Independence Day observances at Lok Bhavan. In Shillong, the festivities are extended beyond the main ceremonial programme. Lok Bhavan will remain open to the public on August 15 and 16, allowing visitors to experience cultural performances by artistes and troupes from Meghalaya and other parts of the country. In Manipur , a state-level function was held at the 1st Manipur Rifles Parade Ground in Imphal West, where Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh hoisted the National Flag. Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Khemchand appealed to all sections of society to rebuild mutual trust and live peacefully. Acknowledging the Central Government’s support in restoring normalcy, he emphasised that lasting stability and development can only be achieved through mutual trust, justice, and the participation of all communities. In Bihar, the main state-level function held at the historic Gandhi Maidan in Patna, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary unfurled the national flag and took the salute of the parade. On the occasion, the Chief Minister announced the formation of a high-level committee headed by a Patna High Court judge to monitor competitive examinations and ensure greater transparency in the examination process. In Ladakh, the 80th Independence Day was celebrated with patriotic fervour and enthusiasm at Khree Sultan Choo Sports Stadium in Kargil, where CEC LAHDC Kargil, Dr. Mohd Jaffer Akhone, hoisted the National Flag and took salute on an impressive March Past. Akashvani Kargil celebrated the 80th Independence Day with patriotic fervour at its Baroo premises, where Head of Office Er. Jamuna Prasad hoisted the National Flag. Officers, officials, their family members and children from adjoining areas participated in the ceremony with enthusiasm.

national_raw_news.title: All India Radio Code
national_raw_news.content: Play Audio Morning News Criticism of friendly countries Attack on religions or communities Anything obscene or defamatory Incitement to violence or anything against maintenance of law & order Anything amounting to contempt of court Aspersions against the integrity of the President, Governors and the Judiciary. Attack on a political party by name Hostile criticism of any State or the Center Anything showing disrespect to the Constitution or advocating change in the Constitution by violence; but advocating changes in a constitutional way should not be debarred. Appeal for funds except for the Prime Ministers National Relief Fund, at a time of External Emergency or if the Country is faced with a natural calamity such a floods, earthquake or cyclone. Direct publicity for or on behalf of an individual or organization which is likely to benefit only that individual or organization. Trade names in broadcasts which amount to advertising directly (except in Commercial Services). The code applies to criticism in the nature of personal tirade either of a friendly Government or of political party or of the Central Government or any State Government. But it does not debar reference to and/or dispassionate discussion of policies pursued by any of them. If a Station Director finds that the above Code has not been respected in any particular by an intending broadcaster he will draw the latters attention to the passage objected to. If the intending broadcaster refuses to accept the Station Directors suggestions and modify his accordingly, the Station Director will be justified in refusing his or her broadcast. Cases of unresolved differences of opinion between a Minister of State Government and the Station Director about the interpretation of the Code with regard to a talk to be broadcast by the former will be referred to the Minister of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India who will decide finally whether or not any change in the text of the talk is necessary in order to avoid violation of the Code. The Election Commission (EC) recognises the significance of television and radio in the coverage of elections. Their reach is widespread and impact substantial. On the one hand, the electronic media can be misused to favour one party or another. But on the other hand, the EC recognises that electronic media can, if used properly be an important source of information for voters across the country. It can provide the widest first hand education for voters on political parties, their symbols, various leaders and different issues in the election. This is why electronic media all over the world is the single biggest source of information of voters in terms of debates, campaign, coverage etc. It is essential therefore that a model code of conduct is established for electronic media both to ensure that it is not misused as well as to ensure that it be used in the best interest of democracy and the voter. national_raw_news.title: News Services Division
national_raw_news.content: Play Audio Morning News Living up to its noble ideals of “Bahujan Hitaya, Bahujan Sukhaya”, the News Services Division (NSD) of AIR strives to provide news and views to every dweller in this vast country in varied terrains, 24X7, in all major languages and dialects, while adhering to highest professional ethics and standards in Radio Broadcasting. The News Services Division is headed by a Director General (News), who is one of the senior most officers of the Indian Information Service. He is assisted by a team of Additional Directors General (News), Directors (News) and Joint Directors (News), Deputy Directors (News), Asstt. Directors (News), News Editors and Reporters etc. The different operational wings of NSD at headquarters in Delhi include: General News Room, Hindi News Room, Reporting Unit, Talks and Current Affairs Unit, Newsreel Unit, Indian Language Units, Reference and PP&D Unit, IT & Website unit and Administrative Wing. The Regional News Units in various States are headed by an officer of the rank of Director or Deputy Director/Assistant Director and assisted by News Editors, Reporters and Newsreaders-cum-Translators. The history of news broadcasting in India is much older than that of All India Radio. The first news bulletin in the country went on the air from the Bombay Station on July 23, 1927 under a private company, the Indian Broadcasting Company. A month later on August 26, 1927 another bulletin in Bengali was started from the Calcutta Station. Until 1935, two bulletins, one each in English and Hindustani were broadcast from Bombay and a bulletin in Bengali was broadcast from Calcutta. The Indian Broadcasting Company went into liquidation in March, 1930 following which broadcasting came under the direct control of the Government of India. The service was designated as the Indian State Broadcasting Service. It was renamed All India Radio on June 8, 1936. The real breakthrough in news broadcasting came after January 1936 when the first news bulletin from the Delhi Station went on the air on January 19, 1936 coinciding with the starting of its transmission. Besides, news bulletins in English and Hindustani, talks on current affairs were also started from the Station in both the languages. The Central News Organization was set up on August 1, 1937. Mr. Charles Barnes took charge as the first News Editor in September and he later became the first Director of News. The outbreak of the Second World War in 1939 gave an impetus to the development of the Organization. The Monitoring Service was set up in 1939 to monitor foreign broadcasts. In 1943, the External Broadcast Unit was set up under the Director of News. By 1945, the Central News Organization was handling news bulletins in different Indian languages as well as in the External Services. After Independence, news broadcasts of AIR grew both in quantity and quality. More emphasis was laid on national and regional news bulletins. The bulk of AIR news comes from its own Correspondents spread all over the country. It has regular Correspondents in India and abroad...

national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Defence ‘Raksha Shakti’ key to achieving the goal of Viksit Bharat, says Prime Minister in his 2026 Independence Day address India must become global supplier of next-gen defence tech: Shri Narendra Modi Need to focus on indigenous defence equipment & enhancing military capabilities in present evolving times: PM Work on Mission Sudarshan Chakra progressing rapidly: Prime Minister Huge voluntary force of civil defence to be created to overcome modern challenges: PM प्रविष्टि तिथि: 15 AUG 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi ‘Raksha Shakti’ is among the seven streams of power outlined by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in his 2026 Independence Day address to the nation, as key to building a Viksit Bharat by 2047. From the ramparts of the Red Fort in Delhi on August 15, 2026, the Prime Minister emphasised the need for Aatmanirbharta in defence and called for India to emerge as a global supplier of next-generation defence technologies. “There is no alternative to being self-reliant in defence. When countries around the world are increasingly thinking about their own interests, Bharat cannot simply remain a market for the world. We must develop drones and counter-drone systems, and take leadership in hypersonic defence technologies,” said the Prime Minister. Reiterating the Government’s resolve to realise the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, Shri Narendra Modi asserted that the nation should no longer live by depending on other countries. “There may be many things available in the world that are cheaper and can be obtained more quickly. But relying on them does not build our own capabilities, nor does it test the strength of our capabilities. Therefore, we must strengthen our own capacities and protect our own interests ourselves. That is why we are moving forward with a firm resolve for ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’. The hearts of Indians are connecting with initiatives like Make in India, Swadeshi, Vocal for Local,” he said. The Prime Minister added that cybersecurity is also an area of defence where the nation can harness the capabilities of the youth for the benefit of the country and the world. Shri Narendra Modi underscored the need to focus on indigenous defence equipment while enhancing the capabilities of the defence forces to stay prepared in the current changing times. “The nature of warfare is changing today; there is no longer a guarantee that conflict will be confined to the borders. Modern warfare can target refineries, the banking sector, or data centers, in a sense, a new form of combat where infrastructure and factories are being destroyed. We announced ‘Mission Sudarshan Chakra’ some years ago, and work on it is progressing rapidly,” he said. Highlighting the transformation witnessed in the defence sector in the last 12 years, the Prime Minister stated that defence production has increased nearly fourfold. He added that defence exports have risen by almost 50 times, with Indian weapons reaching about 100 countries. “Whether the challenge is within or beyond the borders, India is prepared for any situation… India’s reputation is gradually increasing on the global stage,” he...

national_raw_news.title: Anand Vihar, Udhna Railway Stations To Get Large Passenger Holding Areas Before Festival Rush
national_raw_news.content: Anand Vihar, Udhna Railway Stations To Get Large Passenger Holding Areas Before Festival Rush Infrastructure Anand Vihar, Udhna Railway Stations To Get Large Passenger Holding Areas Before Festival Rush Swarajya Staff Aug 15, 2026 | Updated 03:18 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Proposed Anand Vihar passenger holding area (Pic Via Ministry of Railways/PIB) Indian Railways has accelerated work on passenger holding areas at Anand Vihar Terminal and Udhna Railway Station, with completion targeted before the forthcoming major festival rush. Union Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw reviewed the progress yesterday (14 August) from Rail Bhawan, New Delhi, with Union Minister of State for Railways V Somanna also present. The review focused on expediting ongoing works, addressing site-related challenges and ensuring timely completion of the facilities. It covered civil works, removal of obstructions, utility shifting, structural works, passenger amenities and other associated facilities. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras are to be completed before the forthcoming major festival rush to provide safer, more organised and passenger-centric arrangements. At Anand Vihar Terminal, the facility is being developed in two phases . Phase-I will provide organised space for approximately 4,000 passengers, with work on foundations, plinth beams, structural steel fabrication and other associated activities progressing at a fast pace. Phase-II will further strengthen the facility's passenger-handling capacity, enabling it to accommodate around 7,000 passengers on completion. At Udhna Railway Station, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra is planned to accommodate around 15,000 passengers at a time. Significant progress has already been achieved at site, and after completion, the station will provide improved connectivity between the holding area and the platforms, supporting the orderly movement of passengers and better management of passenger flows. The facilities will provide spacious covered waiting and seating areas, dedicated ticketing facilities, toilets for men and women, drinking water and other essential amenities. Public Address and passenger information systems, CCTV surveillance and security arrangements, adequate lighting, electrical facilities, display boards, signage, organised passenger circulation and furniture are also being provided. The holding areas are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers, helping decongest station platforms, circulating areas and station approaches during peak periods. Defence Squadron Leader Sudhir Kumar, who recovered Su-30MKI jet from definite crash, awarded Shaurya Chakra On 9 September, 2025, Squadron Leader Kumar saved his fighter & guided a trainee pilot in front cockpit after a multiple-system failure during a night-time sortie. Snehesh Alex Philip 15 August, 2026 02:57 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Shaurya Chakra awardee Squadron Leader Sudhir Kumar | PIB Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ New Delhi: Squadron Leader Sudhir Kumar, a Su-30MKI pilot who saved his fighter from what could have been potentially a catastrophic crash after a multiple-system failure during a night-time sortie, has been awarded the Shaurya Chakra for his exceptional gallantry and airmanship. Shaurya Chakra is India’s third highest peacetime gallantry award. On 9 September, 2025, Squadron Leader Kumar—a supervisor with more than 1,300 hours of flying experience—was flying as captain of the Su-30MKI aircraft for a low-flying, low-level navigation sortie at night from the rear cockpit, accompanied by an under-training pilot in the front cockpit. Show Full Article During the recovery phase, at an altitude of 2.2 km and a speed of 740 kmph, the aircraft experienced a catastrophic failure that manifested as violent oscillations in the longitudinal plane, accompanied by multiple indicators of a Fly By Wire (FBW) system failure. This resulted in drastic pitch variations ranging from +45 degrees to -15 degrees, extreme g-loads spanning from -1.5 g to +12 g, along with Angle of Attack (AOA) indications exceeding 24 units. Despite experiencing physical forces that exceeded normative limits for human tolerance with extreme conditions of rapidly varying g-loads and pitch, Kumar swiftly took control of the situation and instructed the front pilot to reset the failed FBW channels. national_raw_news.title: Government Removes 12-Minute Advertisement Duration Cap for Television Channels - PIB
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Government Removes 12-Minute Advertisement Duration Cap for Television Channels Ad Duration Cap Removed to Enable Fair Competition and Ensure Ease of Doing Business Posted On: 14 AUG 2026 8:39PM by PIB Delhi The Government has decided to remove the 12-minute advertisement duration cap for television channels. The advertisement duration cap for Television was introduced in the year 2006 under the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994. Since then, the TV broadcasting sector has undergone significant changes. In 2006, there were only 62 TV channels, compared to more than 900 channels at present. At that time, Cable TV, the main platform for delivering TV channels, was analog and had limited carriage capacity, offering consumers very limited choice. Following the complete digitization of the Cable TV sector, all TV distribution platforms, including DTH, Cable TV, HITS and IPTV, are now digital. These platforms currently carry 300 and 500 channels or more, meeting diverse consumer needs and enabling greater variety. Consequently, there is now adequate competition in market dynamics. In view of the changes that have occurred in the TV broadcasting sector, a need was felt to revisit the stipulations relating to advertisement duration. In India, the sector is heavily dependent on advertising, irrespective of whether a channel is ‘pay’ or ‘free-to-air’. Furthermore, there was a non-level playing field for traditional TV channels vis-à-vis digital media, where no such stipulation on advertisement cap regulation exists. The Ministry of I&B is of the view that there exists adequate competition in the market within the TV industry and between the TV industry and digital media. The Government has decided to remove the advertisement duration cap to enable fair competition and ensure ease of doing business. The decision shall come into effect from the date of notification of the amendment in the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994 in the Gazette. *** Mahesh Kumar/ Vivek Vishwash (Release ID: 2299626) Visitor Counter : 6878 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Assamese , Bengali , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu , Kannada , Malayalam Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Government Removes 12-Minute Advertisement Duration Cap for Television Channels Ad Duration Cap Removed to Enable Fair Competition and Ensure Ease of Doing Business Posted On: 14 AUG 2026 8:39PM by PIB Delhi The Government has decided to remove the 12-minute advertisement duration cap for television channels. Garhwal Post Home Uttarakhand Dehradun Mussoorie Interview Features Editorials Politics Cinema Sports Home Dehradun PIB Dehradun urges citizens to join ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign Dehradun Uttarakhand SHARE Facebook Twitter Garhwal Post Bureau Dehradun, 13 Aug: The Press Information Bureau (PIB) Dehradun has appealed to all the residents of the state to participate enthusiastically in the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign and reaffirm their collective resolve towards building a developed India. The campaign, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2022, has grown into a mass movement with people across the country taking part in Tiranga yatras, bike and cycle rallies, cultural programmes and other activities that celebrate the national flag and the spirit of patriotism. Addressing the programme, Assistant Director with PIB Dehradun, Sanjeev Sundriyal said that the tricolour is a symbol of national pride and an eternal inspiration to dedicate everything for the country. He urged everyone to join the campaign with zeal and to reiterate their commitment to contribute to the vision of a developed India. He also called upon the officials and staff of Doordarshan Dehradun, Akashvani and PIB Dehradun to actively promote the campaign and encourage citizens to hoist the national flag with pride. Sundriyal expressed happiness that this year the campaign is dedicated to ‘Vande Mataram’ as the nation marks 150 years of the iconic song. He said the tricolour embodies the spirit of the motherland and serves as a constant motivation for every citizen to give their best for the nation. He added that to spread awareness, the Central Bureau of Communication Dehradun under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting will organise programmes in New Tehri highlighting themes such as Partition Horrors and Vande Mataram, showcasing the journey of the national flag, the struggle for independence and the essence of patriotism. On the occasion, staff from Doordarshan Dehradun, Akashvani and PIB Dehradun were also present and collectively pledged to contribute actively towards building a clean, healthy and sustainable India.
